references.text: The elders of Gilead had already offered Jephthah to be their leader if he fought against the Ammonites, and verse 9 is Jephthah's confirmation and condition for this offer.
Gilead's leaders promised that whoever started the fight against the Ammonites would become head over all who lived in Gilead, which is directly linked to Jephthah's demand.
The Spirit of the Lord came upon Jephthah, and he went out against the Ammonites, and the Lord gave them into his hand, fulfilling the condition in verse 9.
The expression 'the Lord will give them into your hand' is also used regarding victory over enemies, as a parallel to the promise that the Lord will give the Ammonites into Jephthah's hand.
Moses instructed Israel that the Lord goes before them to fight against their enemies, the same theology that Jephthah appeals to.
David expressed similar faith that the Lord would give the enemy into his hand, like Jephthah's statement that the Lord will give the Ammonites before him.
The Lord promises to give the enemies into Israel's hand, the same theological theme as Jephthah's condition in the agreement with the elders of Gilead.
